report.answer_text:
A tower crane has three basic motions: it hoists the load up or down, slews (rotates) around the tower, and moves the load closer to or farther from the tower. Here are the main parts of a typical fixed-jib tower crane and what each does. (morrow.com)
| Part | Function |
|---|---|
| Base and foundation | Anchor the crane and transfer its forces to the ground or supporting structure. |
| Mast (tower) | The vertical steel structure that gives the crane its height and supports the rotating assembly. |
| Slewing unit | Uses a bearing and drive to rotate the upper assembly around the mast. |
| Jib (working arm) | The long horizontal arm that gives the crane its reach and provides a track for the trolley. |
| Trolley | Travels along the jib to move the hook closer to or farther from the mast. |
| Hoist winch and wire rope | The winch winds or unwinds the rope to raise or lower the hook. |
| Hook block | The hanging assembly that contains the hook and usually one or more pulleys. The hook connects to the load’s lifting gear. |
| Counter-jib | The shorter arm opposite the working jib. It supports the counterweights and often carries the hoist machinery. |
| Counterweights | Offset the turning effect of the working jib and load, helping keep the crane stable. |
| Operator’s cab and controls | Provide the operator with a station to control and monitor crane movements. |
These components are shown in Morrow’s illustrated tower crane guide. (morrow.com)
Key difference: A fixed-jib crane changes its reach by moving the trolley. A luffing-jib crane changes its reach by raising or lowering the jib itself. (morrow.com)
